findings.summary: The RF2 profile wrapper needs job-level attachment and matching completion windows across daemon restarts.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/65/design.md:77-84 proposes an outer campaign wrapper with PID-start checking but does not define attachment/window hooks. scripts/lab.sh:1857-1870 stops the node during every write_reset, and write_volume:1884-1886 starts a new daemon. The campaign invokes measured jobs at :2060 and :2074, with whole-disk writes, preconditioning and idle at :2063-2068 and integrity/restart work at :2094 between measured jobs. Attaching once around the campaign profiles a dead PID after the first reset; attaching for a broad campaign interval instead mixes unrelated operations into CPU/sample numerators. PID-reuse rejection alone does not repair either case, so S4/S5 CPU per successful durable I/O is not reproducible as designed.
findings.fix: Specify opt-in hooks immediately around each selected fio measurement after write_reset/write_volume, reacquire and validate target/peer PID-start identities per window, wait for profiler readiness, and retain that window's successful completion count/bytes and interval along with its profiles. Stop before preconditioning, idle, integrity and restart, and invalidate interrupted/missing windows rather than combining them with another round's denominator. Keep existing reset/integrity/restore semantics. Add fake campaign tests with PID changes across resets, unrelated precondition/integrity CPU, failed attach and partial/resumed jobs.

findings.summary: Endpoint thread CPU alone does not account for the kernel-network CPU that the comparison is intended to measure.
findings.evidence: spec.md S4 requires accounting for shared/idle CPU and attribution to kernel TCP. design.md:55-67 defines CPU ns/op only from endpoint thread CPU clocks and makes perf optional; its shared/cgroup/host background accounting is specified only for the separate RF2 campaign at :80. TCP may execute receive/softirq work outside the endpoint threads (for example ksoftirqd), and async I/O helpers may run elsewhere. Thread CPU clocks and perf attached only to those TIDs exclude that work rather than putting it in the unknown bucket. In contrast memory streams remove kernel processing. The resulting paired CPU difference can therefore omit precisely the displaced work while being reported as total endpoint/transport CPU.
findings.fix: Define the accounting boundary explicitly: retain endpoint-thread CPU as a labeled partial metric, record helper threads and a bounded system/CPU-scoped kernel/background observation for local trials, and treat unattributable off-thread work as unknown. Only present a transport-total CPU difference when its accounting coverage is qualified; otherwise report the endpoint-only difference and an inconclusive kernel/total saving. Do not add overlapping thread and system counters. Add an analysis fixture with nonzero off-thread network work and one with unavailable system profiling, verifying neither silently becomes zero or a qualified total.

findings.summary: The optional actual-Net fixture cannot satisfy the stated join-before-exit lifecycle through the current Net API.
findings.evidence: design.md:39-41 includes an optional fixture using actual NetCommand/NetEvent, and :48-51 requires cancel/close/join on failure. flaminio-node/src/net.rs:97-165 spawns a detached OS thread and returns only Net { cmds }; NetCommand::Close at :158-160 cancels an outgoing session, not the network thread or accepting loop. Dropping all Net handles permits eventual thread exit, but gives the harness no join or completion handle. Without a specific benchmark-only lifecycle, repeated fixtures can overlap teardown or leave listeners/tasks alive while later trials start, violating the stated isolation and contaminating counters.
findings.fix: Either omit this optional fixture from the increment or specify a bounded child-process fixture that owns actual Net instances and is awaited/reaped on success, failure and timeout before the next trial. An explicitly scoped dev-only lifecycle mechanism is another option if it leaves product behavior unchanged. Add a fixture test proving no owned process/listener remains after timeout and repeated trials do not overlap.

report: Full R1 review of all four issue-65 intent/spec/design/decisions files, preserving the Nov 13 approved measurement slice and settlements.
